chunks: From him, from Abu Ja'far, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, from some of his teachers, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) issued a ruling regarding a woman whose husband died while she was pregnant, and she gave birth before four months and ten days had passed, and she married before completing the four months and ten days. He ruled that she should be divorced, and then he should not propose to her until the end of the two periods (of waiting). If the woman's guardians wish, they may marry her off, and if they wish, they may keep her, and return his dowry to him.

key_terms.أَرْبَعَةُ أَشْهُرٍ وَ عَشْرٌ: Four months and ten days (the waiting period for a pregnant woman)
key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.الْأَجَلَيْنِ: The two periods (referring to the period of pregnancy and the subsequent period after birth)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pregnant widow who remarries before completing the four months and ten days of waiting period?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam Ali (AS) establishes the principle of 'Iddah al-Wad' (waiting period for pregnancy) overlapping with 'Iddah al-Talaq' (waiting period for divorce), ensuring the widow's lineage is clear before finalizing a new marriage. It highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence where the guardian (Awliya) may choose to retain the new husband or return the dowry, reflecting a pragmatic approach to social stability and financial rights.
